newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT--Morrison named Campbell Soup CEO.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT--Morrison named Campbell Soup CEO.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co said Monday it named Dale Morrison president and chief executive officer. David Johnson will remain chairman until July 31, 1998.
A full text of the company's press release follows.

CAMDEN, N.J., June 30 /PRNewswire/ -- Campbell Soup Company (NYSE: CPB) announced today that Dale F. Morrison, 48, President -- International and Specialty Foods, will become President and Chief Executive Officer effective July 15, 1997. Morrison will succeed David W. Johnson, 64. Johnson will continue as Chairman of the Company and Chairman of the Board's Executive Committee until July 31, 1998.

Campbell also announced that Basil L. Anderson, 52, Chief Financial Officer, and Robert F. Bernstock, 46, President -- U.S. Grocery, will each be promoted from Senior Vice President to Executive Vice President of the Company, also effective July 15, 1997.

"Campbell's strength has always come from team power," said Johnson. "Our new senior executive team is outstanding in both talent and partnership. Dale Morrison is a proven team leader and a superb executive. His general manager experience includes six years of international assignments and features a track record of profitable sales growth. Bob Bernstock provides a relentless focus and flair for innovation which has been critical to Campbell's global leadership in soup. Basil Anderson is a world-class and strategic CFO who makes a large and measurable difference in our company."

Commenting on his continuing role as Chairman, Johnson said, "My priority is to ensure that we continue our relentless commitment to building shareowner wealth. I will assist Dale in exploring the strategies needed to achieve Campbell's vision of becoming the best consumer products company in the world."

Morrison joined Campbell in June 1995 as President of Pepperidge Farm, where he led a dramatic turnaround of the business. Between 1990 and 1995 Pepperidge Farm sales grew only about 2 percent. By the end of the July 31, 1996, fiscal year sales increased 10 percent. Sales this year are up 13 percent so far this year. Profits have increased more than 20 percent both years. Morrison's approach, which blended cost savings with investments in marketing icon brands such as "Goldfish" crackers and "Milano" cookies, is now being carried out across the entire Campbell Soup Company.

Morrison was appointed President -- International and Specialty Foods in November 1996, overseeing International Grocery, Global Food Service, Frozen and Specialty Foods, and Bakery and Confectionery divisions.

Prior to joining Campbell, Morrison spent 14 years with PepsiCo Inc. in both the soft drink and snack foods divisions of the company. As President -- Frito Lay North and Canada, a $1.7 billion revenue division of Frito-Lay North America, Morrison developed the long-term strategy that helped to make Frito- Lay North PepsiCo's number one growth division in 1995. As Managing Director of Walkers Smiths Snackfoods Ltd. in the U.K., Morrison led the successful integration and growth of the $750 million revenue businesses PepsiCo acquired from RJR Nabisco in 1989. Market share has grown substantially, operating profit has risen dramatically and the division is now one of PepsiCo's most profitable international businesses.

Morrison began his career at General Foods where he worked from 1971 to 1981. He is a native of North Dakota and a 1971 graduate of the University of North Dakota. He and his wife Barbara have two children.

Morrison said, "I am proud and excited about the opportunity to lead one of the world's best consumer companies. Because of David Johnson's leadership, Campbell's brands and its people are strong. David has instilled a passion for building shareowner wealth across the company. I share that passion. I am ready and eager to lead our people and our brands to new heights. I am fully committed to driving our Strategic Growth Plan to address Campbell's two biggest challenges -- building profitable sales growth and expanding our international business. Campbell's opportunities both in the U.S. and overseas are limitless. With the support of Bob Bernstock, Basil Anderson and the entire Campbell team, I have high confidence that we can accelerate our winning momentum."

The Campbell succession process began last year with the appointment of a special committee of independent directors led by Philip E. Lippincott, former chairman and CEO of Scott Paper Co. Other members included Bennett Dorrance, grandson of Campbell's founder, Dr. John T. Dorrance and president of DMB Associates, a real estate development firm, Harvey Golub, chairman and CEO of American Express Company, and Charles H. Mott, president and CEO of the leading investment management firm John W. Bristol & Co.

The committee worked closely with Johnson and the entire Campbell Board in testing and measuring candidates. As part of the exhaustive search process, the committee retained Thomas J. Neff, Chairman of Spencer Stuart Associates, to identify the best qualified external candidates.

"Accountability to our shareowners was the guiding force in our selection process," Lippincott said. "Our mandate was to find the most qualified candidate available. We set high standards and developed extensive criteria to measure every candidate. We interviewed very strong finalists, several of them from outside the company. We were unanimous in our decision that Dale Morrison is the clear first choice.

"The story of David Johnson and Campbell Soup has been a legendary business success. Campbell's record in the 90s on all key financial measures is unrivaled in the food industry. Since David was named to lead the Company in January 1990, Campbell's total return to shareowners has been 23 percent a year. Market value has more than tripled. With Dale, Bob, Basil and David leading the way, we are fully confident that record will only get better."
